title: Maintain a declared inventory of the routes intended to be indexable
statement: The repository holds an explicit, machine-readable statement of which routes are meant to be indexable, and the set of routes actually serving indexable responses matches it.
rationale: Without a declaration there is nothing for a change to contradict, so indexability drift produced by a template edit, a new route, or a build flag has no detectable signature and every later check has to guess what the intent was.
implementation: Derive the inventory from the route definitions the framework already exposes, annotate each entry as indexable or excluded, and store the result in the repository. Treat a mismatch between the inventory and the served responses as a failure of one of the two, decided by which one states the intent.

verification.method: Diff the declared inventory against the routes whose served responses permit indexing, reporting entries present on only one side.

title: Keep authenticated and administrative routes out of the index
statement: Routes that require a session, an account, or an administrative role are excluded from indexing, and their exclusion does not depend on the login redirect happening to hide them.
rationale: An account or admin route that reaches the index exposes the surface of the private area and produces results a visitor cannot use, and a redirect-based defence fails the moment a route renders a shell before checking the session.
implementation: Serve an index-suppressing directive from the authenticated layout itself so every route beneath it inherits it, and return 401 or 404 rather than a rendered shell for an unauthenticated request. Do not rely on robots.txt alone, since a blocked path can still be listed from external links.

verification.method: Request a representative set of account and admin paths without credentials and record the status, robots directives, and whether any private content appears.

title: Block indexing of non-production hosts
statement: Preview, staging, and branch deployment hosts serve an index-suppressing directive on every response, and that suppression is driven by the environment rather than by a file the production build also carries.
rationale: Preview hosts serve the same content as production, so once indexed they compete with it directly, and a suppression mechanism shared with the production build eventually ships to production and removes the real site instead.
implementation: Key the directive on a deployment-provided environment value, emitted as a response header at the edge so it covers non-HTML responses too. Verify the production host does not match the condition before deploying, and prefer access control over indexing directives where the preview content is confidential.

verification.method: Request the same path on a preview host and on the production host and compare the robots directives returned by each.

title: Exclude internal search result pages from the index
statement: URLs produced by the site's own search feature are not indexable, are not linked with crawlable hrefs, and do not appear in any sitemap.
rationale: A search route generates an address for every query anyone can type, and the resulting pages hold only excerpts of content that already exists elsewhere on the site, so indexing them adds copies rather than pages.
implementation: Emit the index-suppressing directive from the search route handler itself, and render result links without exposing the query URL as a crawlable destination. Curated landing pages that happen to use the search backend are a separate case and stay indexable on purpose.

verification.method: Request the search route with a query string and record the robots directives on the response together with whether the path appears in the sitemap.

title: Suppress indexing of pages that render no substantive content
statement: A route that legitimately returns 200 but has nothing to show - an empty collection, a profile with no entries, a placeholder awaiting content - is excluded from indexing until it holds content.
rationale: Pages with no content of their own are treated as thin, and a template that can generate thousands of them turns a single empty state into a large share of what the engine sees of the site.
implementation: Have the route decide indexability from the size of the result set it rendered, suppressing the index directive when the set is empty. Where the empty state is permanent rather than temporary, return 404 instead so the URL leaves the index rather than staying as an excluded entry.

verification.method: Request a route known to have an empty result set and record its status, robots directives, and the amount of unique text in the response.

caution: There is no published threshold that separates thin from substantive content, so this control identifies pages with no content of their own rather than pages below a measured size.

title: State the indexability of paginated pages explicitly
statement: The site records whether pages after the first in a sequence are meant to be indexable, and the directives those pages serve match that decision uniformly across the whole sequence.
rationale: Sequences are commonly left half-configured, with the first page indexable and later pages inconsistently suppressed, which makes the items that appear only on later pages reachable in one configuration and invisible in another.
implementation: Choose one policy per sequence type and apply it from the shared pagination component. If later pages are suppressed, confirm the items they list are reachable from somewhere that is indexable, otherwise those items have no discovery path at all.

verification.method: Fetch several pages of one sequence and record the robots directives on each, then compare them against the recorded policy for that sequence.
